title: Placenta anatomy: villi, maternal and fetal blood, and umbilical cord
description: Examine decidua, chorionic villi, separate maternal and fetal circulations, placental exchange, membranes and the three-vessel cord.

questions.question: Do maternal and fetal blood directly mix in the normal placenta?
questions.answer: No. Maternal blood in intervillous spaces surrounds villi containing fetal capillaries. Gases and substances cross a changing tissue barrier rather than flowing through a single shared open blood vessel.

questions.question: How many vessels does an umbilical cord normally have?
questions.answer: Usually there are two umbilical arteries carrying fetal blood toward the placenta and one umbilical vein returning from placenta toward the fetus. Individual anatomy requires clinical assessment.

questions.question: Which placenta parts come from mother and fetus?
questions.answer: The uterine decidua basalis forms the maternal attachment bed, while fetal chorionic villi and chorionic plate form the fetal exchange structures. The amnion covers the fetal-facing side.

questions.question: What happens across chorionic villi?
questions.answer: Fetal capillaries run inside villi exposed to surrounding maternal intervillous blood. Oxygen, nutrients and wastes transfer across placental tissue; the illustration cannot measure exchange efficiency.

questions.question: When is the placenta delivered in childbirth?
questions.answer: After the baby is born, the placenta and membranes are delivered during the third stage of labor. The anatomy image depicts an attached placenta during pregnancy, not its actual separation.
